g1.label: 1. A Full English is usually eaten…
g1.why: The text says a Full English is normally a weekend meal, not an everyday breakfast.

g2.label: 2. Black pudding is made from…
g2.why: Despite the name, black pudding is a savoury sausage of blood and oats — there is no chocolate in it.

g3.label: 3. The most popular weekday lunch
g3.why: During the working week most people eat a quick sandwich; the roast is a Sunday meal.

g4.correct: a crispy batter served with roast beef
accept: a crispy batter served with roast beef
g4.label: 4. Yorkshire pudding is…
g4.why: Yorkshire pudding is savoury: a crispy baked batter eaten with roast beef, not a dessert.

g5.label: 5. One of Britain’s most popular dishes
g5.why: Chicken tikka masala is so widely eaten in Britain that it is often called a national dish.

g6.label: 6. British people drink tea with…
g6.why: Tea in Britain is normally taken with milk; lemon is more usual elsewhere.

g1.label: 1. Yorkshire pudding is made from a crispy ___
g1.why: Batter is the liquid flour-and-egg mixture that bakes crisp.

g2.label: 2. A Full English is very ___
g2.why: “Filling” means it makes you feel full — which is why no lunch is needed afterwards.

g3.label: 3. Bangers and ___ potato
g3.why: Mashed potato is crushed smooth; “bangers and mash” is sausages with mashed potato.

g4.label: 4. Brown sauce over meat and potatoes
g4.why: Gravy is the brown sauce made from meat juices and poured over a roast.

g5.label: 5. The tomatoes are usually ___
g5.why: Grilled means cooked under direct heat, which is how the tomatoes are done.

g6.label: 6. Many people order a ___ on Friday
g6.why: A takeaway is food ordered to eat at home instead of cooking.

g7.label: 7. At afternoon tea people eat ___
g7.why: Scones with cream and jam are the classic afternoon-tea cake.

g8.label: 8. Thin fried potato slices in a bag
g8.why: In British English these are crisps; “chips” means something different here.
